title: Environmental/project-facility compliance — FY2017 Section 5339 evidence
summary: The FY2017 Section 5339 binder documents STIP inclusion, useful-life controls for grant-funded assets, labor acceptance, no-displacement certification, project-specific NEPA disposition, and RTEC's environmental policy/management responsibilities.

claims.claim: For the FY2017 Section 5339 project, RTEC stated that MPO TIP inclusion was not applicable because it served rural Southeast Kentucky and that RTEC was included in the STIP.

Grant-funded capital purchases were to remain RTEC-owned and in service for their useful life; if sold or devoted to another use during useful life, RTEC would refund a proportionate federal share based on fair-market-value proceeds.

evidence.page_or_section: PDF page 71 / Use of Project Facilities/Equipment

claims.claim: RTEC certified that no persons, families, or businesses would be displaced by the proposed FY2017 project.
The binder marked anticipation of NEPA requirements as not applicable to this project while acknowledging FTA environmental-review obligations for future proposed projects.
RTEC characterized the project as a Class 2 action with no significant environmental impact and documented an environmental policy integrating environmental management into business activities.

trigger: Grant-funded capital project or activity requiring environmental/project-facility review.
actors: FTA Regional Office / regional environmental review roles
steps: Document ownership/useful-life obligations for grant-funded assets.
Apply RTEC environmental policy and committee review where environmental concerns arise.
controls: Environmental Protection Committee described as a recurring forum for concerns/recommendations.
unresolved_questions: Does RTEC still maintain an Environmental Protection Committee?
What current environmental/NEPA review workflow supersedes this FY2017 policy?
Where are current useful-life and disposition records for federally funded assets maintained?
